div.l: And yet he was but esy of despense
He kepte that he wan in pestilence
For gold in phisyk is accordiall
Therfor he loved gold in especiall
A gode wyf ther was bysyde Bathe
But she was somdel def and þat was scathe
Of cloth makyng she had suche an haunte
She passed hem of ypres and of gawnte
In all the paryssh wyf ne was ther none
That to offeryng to forne hir shuld gone
And if ther dede shortely wroth was she
That she was out of alle charite
Hir keủerches full fyne were of ground
I durst swere they weyed x pound
Whan on sonday wern on hir hed
Hir hosen were of fyne scarlet
Full streyght I teyed and chōmse full soft and newe
Bolde was hir face and faire and red of hewe
She was a worthy woman all hr hir lyve
Husbondes at the chirche door she had fyve
With outen other compayny in thought
But ther of nedeth nat to speke right nowght
And thryes had she ben at Ihrlm̄Ierusalem
She had passed many a strong streme
At Rome she had ben̄ and at Boloigne
In Galys at seynt Iamys and at Coloigne
She cowde moche on wandryng by the weye
Gat tothed was she sothly for to seye
Vp on an Ambeler sothly she satte
Y wympled wee and on hir hed an hatte
As brode as is a bokeler or a targe
A fote mantel a bout hir hepys large
And on hir feet a payr of spores sharpe
In felaship weel coude she lawgh and carpe
Of remedyes of love she knewe ꝑper chaunce
For she coude of that arte the olde daunce
A gode man was ther of religioıı̄un
And was a ꝑpersoūn of a toun̄
But riche he was of holy thought and werk
He was also a lerned man̄ and ls a a ls a a Clerk
Þat Cristes gospell truly wold preche
His parisshons deuoutely wold he teche
Benigne he was and wonder diligente
And in adủersyte he was full paciente
And so was he ꝓproved often sythes
Full loth were hym to curs for his tythes
But rather wolde he yeuen out of doute
Vn to his pore parisshons a boute
Of hise offrynges and of his substaunce
So coude he in litel thyng haue suffisaunce
Wyde was hise parish and housez fer a sundre
But he ne laft nouther for reyne ne for thundre
In sikenesse ne in mys cheef for to Visite
The ferthest in his parish bothe moche and lite
Vpon his feet and in his honde a stānf
Þis noble example to his sheep he yaf
Þat first he wrout and afterward þat he taught
Out of the gospel he thoo wordes caught
And this figure he had eke therto
That if gold ruste what shuld yron do
For if a preest be foule on whom we truste
No wondre is it a lewde man to ruste
And shame it is if a preest take kepe
A shiten sheepherd and a clene shepe
Weel ought a preest example for to yeve
By his clennesse how this his sheep shuld lyve
He set nat his benefice to hyre
And lete his sheep to be acombred in þe myre
And ranne to londoūn to seynt Poules
To seke hym a chauntrye for soules
Or with a bretherode to be witholde
But duelled at hom and kept his folde
So þat þe wolf ne made it to mys carye
He was a sheperd and nat a Mercenarye
And if he were holy and vertuous
He was nat to synfull men despitous
Ne of speche daungerous ne digne
But in his speche discrete and benigne
To drawen folk to heuene by fairenesse
By gode exaumple this was his besynesse
But if it were any ꝑpersone obstynate
What so he were of high or lowe estate
Hym wolde he snybbe sharpely for þe nones
A better preest I trowe þat nowher none is
He wayted after no pompe ne reuerence
Ne maked hym a spyced concience
But crystes lore and his Apostelys twelve
He taught but first he folwyd hem in hym selve
